title: Amorphous insulating MoS$_x$ films deposited by magnetron sputtering as a low-index optical coating
authors: S. G. Martanov, E. V. Tarkaeva, A. V. Muratov, A. V. Lubenchenko, O. N. Pavlov, A. G. Vitukhnovsky, A. Yu. Kuntsevich
abstract: While much effort are now concentrated on exploration of crystalline form of MoS$_2$ as a two-dimensional material, we show that room-temperature DC magnetron sputtering from pressurized MoS$_2$ powder target produces amorphous MoS$_x$ films with optical properties fundamentally different from those of crystalline MoS$_2$. The films were found to have a sulfur content of approximately $x=1.8$, indicating sulfur deficiency. They are optically isotropic and exhibit rather low optical losses, with a refractive index of about 2 over the visible and near-infrared spectral range. Their compatibility with lift-off lithography and dry etching makes amorphous MoS$_x$ a promising material for integrated photonic applications.
summary: This work demonstrates the successful deposition of amorphous, sulfur-deficient MoS$_x$ films using magnetron sputtering. These films exhibit desirable low-index optical properties and insulating behavior, fundamentally differing from crystalline MoS$_2$. The findings establish amorphous MoS$_x$ as a promising, easily fabricated material for advanced integrated photonic devices.
main_problem: To characterize amorphous MoS$_x$ films deposited by magnetron sputtering as a viable, low-index optical coating alternative to crystalline MoS$_2$.
main_result: The resulting amorphous MoS$_x$ films are optically isotropic, possess a low refractive index ($\approx 2$), and exhibit insulating behavior, making them promising for integrated photonics.
method: The study employed magnetron sputtering for deposition, followed by comprehensive characterization using XRD, XPS, ellipsometry, and AFM.
model_or_system: The physical system is the amorphous insulating MoS$_x$ film, deposited from a MoS$_2$ target, which is chemically characterized as sulfur-deficient ($	ext{MoS}_{1.8}$).
key_observables: Refractive index ($n \approx 2$), optical losses, sulfur deficiency ($x=1.8$), insulating sheet resistance, and surface oxidation rate ($\approx 0.3 	ext{ nm/week}$).
important_parameters: Deposition pressure ($\approx 6-7	imes 10^{-2} 	ext{ mbar}$), spectral range ($400-1500 	ext{ nm}$), and ambient oxidation time (up to 2 weeks).
main_assumptions: The insulating nature is attributed to the amorphous state and sulfur deficiency, keeping the concentration below the percolation threshold for conductivity.
figures_summary: Figures show XRD patterns confirming amorphous structure, AFM topography comparing bare Si to coated samples, and XPS/Ellipsometry data comparing the film's optical constants to bulk crystalline MoS$_2$.
paper_structure: The paper details the sputtering process and characterization techniques, presents results showing the amorphous nature and low optical index, discusses the oxidation dynamics, and concludes by positioning the material for photonic applications.
why_interesting: While the focus is materials science, the study of amorphous films and their electronic/optical properties touches upon concepts relevant to disordered systems, such as localization and band structure modification due to disorder.
